svg.data-depth-with-handles: 518.9 mm over fan and power-supply handles (Table 19; drawing g009881 reads 518.4)
svg.data-psu-ac-input: dedicated feed per inlet; breaker min 20 A at 110 VAC or 16 A at 220 VAC
svg.data-psu-dc-input: PS0 from feed A, PS1 from feed B (A/B redundancy)
svg.data-max-thermal-output: 1705 BTU/hour (500 W) (Table 20; provisioning ceiling, not reconciled with the 280 W maximum draw)
svg.data-operating-temp: 0 C to 40 C normal; -5 C to 55 C short-term (NEBS GR-63-CORE Issue 4 short-term, up to 96 h, max 15 days/year)
svg.data-storage-temp: -40 C to 70 C in shipping container
svg.data-storage: 100-GB SATA SSD (Routing Engine description; the faceplate carries SSD0 and SSD1 activity LEDs, and no sentence in the guide states the drive count)
svg.data-routing-engine: built-in on the baseboard, not replaceable
svg.data-rate-selectability: each QSFP port runs 100GbE, 40GbE, or 4x10GbE via breakout; QSA adapter (MAM1Q00A-QSA) converts a port to single 10GbE or 1GbE from Junos 18.3R1
svg.data-timing: BITS and ToD RJ45 ports, 1PPS and 10 MHz SMB input and output, PTP grandmaster clock SFP port (GM/PTP)
svg.data-oob: MGMT RJ-45, autosensing 10/100/1000 with link and activity LEDs
svg.data-usb: single USB port (guide names no revision)
svg.data-seismic: Designed to meet Telcordia Technologies Zone 4 earthquake requirements (Table 20 wording, transcribed)

The rack-requirements table says the MOUNTING BRACKETS \"extend the width to 19 in\", yet drawing and table agree the body itself is ~482.3 including the integral ear flanges - this chassis is genuinely full-rack-width, with the front face spanning ear to ear. The modelled width is the 437.0 mm BODY between the ear-flange fold lines (ears are not modelled here - see ears)","color":"photo - light Juniper grey, sampled from mx204-front-high.jpg (#9a9ea3); module faces near-black charcoal, fan furniture orange","drawing-vs-photo":"sources-disagree, and the REAL DEVICE (Juniper studio photographs) wins for everything printed: the guide art labels the QSFP ports 0/0-0/3 and the SFP+ ports 1/0-1/7 (CLI interface names), prints 10MHz / 1PPS on the SMB columns, orders the LED row ...SSD1 SSD0, puts MX204 beside the Juniper logo and a junos badge at the right. The photographed faceplate prints plain 0-3 and 4/5-10/11 port numbers, PPS and 100MHz under the SMB columns, orders the row SSD0 SSD1, prints MX204 at the RIGHT end and carries no junos badge. The silkscreen below follows the photograph; note the guide TEXT unambiguously calls the clock ports 10-MHz (pinout table, clocking topic), so the printed 100MHz legend is carried as artwork while the function stays 10 MHz - see gaps","ears":"NOT MODELLED, by project convention - devices in this library are drawn without rack ears. The MX204's guide art draws integral ear flanges at both ends of both faces (fold lines at x 22.65 and 459.65 on the 482.3 mm rack face, each flange carrying two rounded slots and, on the front, a central 8.2 mm hole), and Table 19's 19 in width is measured over them. The modelled body is the 437.0 mm between the fold lines; all front and rear coordinates were measured on the 482.3 mm drawing and shifted by -22.65. The removable outboard brackets in the photographs are likewise not modelled","esd-front":"drawing + photo - a recessed socket at 31.1, 28.9 with the ESD symbol below; the guide's \"ESD Points\" figure (g009865, Figure 5) marks this same location. The guide art draws it as a hex-nut stud; the photograph shows a plain recessed socket - photo carried","lifecycle":"announced - Juniper lists MX204-HW-BASE end-of-sale 2027-06-15 and end-of-support 2032-06-30 (support.juniper.net M/MX hardware milestones, mirrored by Park Place and router-switch EOL trackers, searched 2026-08-26)","mgmt-block":"drawing - MGMT and BITS RJ45s centred at 267.6/289.7 (y 27.25), CON and ToD at 312.8/336.8 (y 27.4); vertical USB-A at 352.5, 27.8; SMB quad at 366.7/376.5 x 23.8/31.4 (IN row above OUT row); five status lamps at y 34.2, x 387.6 (OK/FAIL), 399.1 (ONLINE), 409.4 (ALM), 417.5, 425.7; recessed OFFLINE button at 435.5 and RESET pinhole at 447.0 (RESET x read off the photograph between OFFLINE and the ear; not resolvable on the drawing - estimated). The drawing draws OFFLINE ~3 mm above the lamp row (31.3 against 34.2); both buttons are MODELLED ON the lamp centreline for visual consistency, a deliberate deviation recorded here","other-faces":"near-blank by evidence - no photograph or drawing of the top, bottom or side faces exists in the intake beyond the g009881 top-view outline, which shows a plain slab with the mounting rails pre-attached along the sides. Each face carries only its rail band(s), estimated and marked so, which is also what lets the capability chain count the face as drawn. Faces are sized from Table 19. Every face carries only symmetric content as far as the sources show, so the axis conventions have been checked but nothing asymmetric pins them. Axis conventions, checked against viewer3d.js: LEFT view x = 0 is the REAR, RIGHT view x = 0 is the FRONT, top and bottom have y = 0 at the FRONT with left/right mirrored between them","port-leds":"photo + drawing - each SFP+ column carries a lamp strip between the rows: triangle-up, two lenses, triangle-down (drawing shows the four marks at y 22.1 with lenses at column-centre +/-1.8). The up triangle ties the left lens to the upper port and the down triangle the right lens to the lower port. NO DOCUMENT DESCRIBES THESE LAMPS: searched the guide doc.md for \"port LED\", \"link and activity\", \"rate-selectable\" near LED, and \"triangle\"; the front-panel LED table (Table 17) covers only system LEDs. States left as the component default, description records the silence. The QSFP ports carry NO per-port faceplate LEDs - confirmed against the photograph, not just the text (the only marks above the cages are vent holes). The GM/PTP port has two stacked lamps at x 63.6 (y 26.6/32.1), also undocumented","port-numbering":"photo - QSFP ports are silkscreened 0-3; SFP+ columns are silkscreened 4/5, 6/7, 8/9, 10/11 with the UPPER number on the upper port (the guide art writes 1/0 over 1/1 the same way up). CLI names (et-0/0/x, xe-0/1/x) are not printed on the metal","ports":"drawing + registry - four QSFP cages centred at x 76.7/95.7/114.7/ 133.7 (measured pitch 18.93, registry qsfp-ganged pitch 19.0), aperture centre y 27.5; eight SFP+ in a 2x4 belly-to-belly block, column centres 158.1/172.3/186.6/200.8 (pitch 14.25 per registry, measured 14.3), row centres y 14.25 and 30.15; GM/PTP SFP centred at 53.15, 29.65 (aperture interior read off the labelled drawing). Counts confirmed by the photograph and the guide text (4 + 8 + 1)","power":"guide power planning - 240 W typical at 25 C and 280 W maximum at 55 C for a fully loaded router (Tables 28 and 31, AC and DC alike; the vendor qualifies both by ambient, not by measure). Table 32 adds the DC INPUT figure at 90% efficiency: 266 W at 25 C; Table 33's 55 C input value fell outside the text layer of this extraction and is not carried. Table 20 separately states maximum thermal output 1705 BTU/hour (500 W) - a different scope (provisioning ceiling) that is transcribed under thermal and deliberately NOT reconciled with the 280 W draw","rear":"drawing (g009862 at the same per-axis scales) + photo - recessed left panel 24-97.7 across the full height carrying the grounding plate (lug circles at 38.6 and 54.6, y 17.2), the earth symbol at 46.6, 31.6 and the ESD socket at 81.4, 17.2 with its symbol above at 81.1, 6.7. Three fan bays with apertures ~42 mm on a 49.1 mm pitch at x 107.8/156.9/206.0, each preceded by a chassis strip printed with a fan icon (y 17.1), the bay number (y 21.6) and the fan status lamp (y 28.9) at x 103.2/152.4/201.2. A blank recessed plate spans 256-327.3. Two PSU bays at 334.9 and 396.3 (apertures measure 57.0, module width 56.6 per Table 19; the bay is sized 42.4 tall for the DC module, the taller of the two occupants per Table 19, so the 40.1 AC face sits in it with clearance), silkscreened 0 and 1 on the chassis left of each bay. A fourth small hole appears at 250.0, 28.9 on the drawing right of fan 2 with no icon or number above it; left unmodelled and recorded here","rear-axis":"the rear view is its own face with x = 0 at ITS left edge (the chassis RIGHT side seen from the front); the fan and PSU modules are horizontal, so nothing mirrors. Positions are direct measurements of the rear drawing, not derived from front coordinates","rj45-orientation":"drawing + photo - CON and ToD are drawn and photographed contacts-UP (keyway down, std/rj45 default); MGMT and BITS are drawn contacts-DOWN with two integrated LED windows at the top corners, so they carry rotate 180 and a lamp pair placed over the top corners. The MGMT lamps are the guide's own \"activity LED and link LED\"; BITS lamp roles (Activity left, Link right) are Table 17's","scale":"drawing - the guide front view (g009860) rendered at 600 dpi measures 2895 x 275 px, aspect 10.53 against the true 482.3/43.7 = 11.04, so the figure is stretched ~4.6% vertically and is SCHEMATIC. All positions below are fractions off it anchored per axis: x at 6.003 px/mm to the 482.3 mm width, y at 6.293 px/mm to the 43.7 mm height. Feature sizes come from the standards registry, never from this drawing. The rear (g009862) is the same art family and was measured the same way","serial-label":"guide Figure 60 shows the chassis serial-number label; its figure crops without a locating dimension and the topic does not name a face.
